items.title: Angled canvas-origin wall drag freezes its preview and quote under the HUD while release orders a longer run
items.body:
## Verified native reproduction

At 1920×1080 in the angled renderer, create and pause a new prison, open Build and arm Brick wall. Start a left-button drag on uncovered canvas and continue to the native Category select inside the right rail without releasing the button. Release above that control.

On unchanged production source at `e44ce410e7`, Full HD 100% and 200% both failed the native diagnostic. The uncovered-map control first submitted exactly its two intended square orders.

| UI scale | canvas start → native Category endpoint | held preview/readout | actual released worker orders |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100% | (1377,237) → (1785.078125,237) | 3 squares from (23,15), catalogue value 240 | exact (23,15)..(27,15): 5 squares, value 400 |
| 200% | (1013,539) → (1706.15625,539) | 3 squares from (16,16), catalogue value 240 | exact (16,16)..(22,16): 7 squares, value 560 |

The issue is a stale construction preview and catalogue quote. Commands are neither truncated nor lost in these measured cases. The native event trace shows canvas-origin pointerdown/mousedown, pointerout with buttons=1 into the HUD, then pointerup/mouseup targeting SELECT. Phaser receives the window mouseup and commits the endpoint, but its canvas mousemove listener stopped updating the held preview at the rail.

## Scope and intended behavior

Top-down canvas-origin drags already retain pointer capture under the HUD (closed #878). The angled scene lacks that acquisition. A canvas-origin armed construction drag should retain its preview through release; a press starting on the Category control should retain its native interaction. Preserve pointercancel/lostcapture cancellation and normal touch release.

This is a distinct native HUD boundary from #1914's stationary pointer after a camera pose change and #1935's cancelled camera turn. Fresh all-state searches for oblique/angled HUD drag, capture and canvas pointerout were read before filing.

Initial baseline: 2/2 red (8.5/6.6s), both at held preview count; a second unchanged-source run with durable passive traces was 2/2 red (6.8/6.4s), at the same 3 versus 5/7 assertion. Source checkpoint `2f0aa78eff` adds scoped capture only for mouse left presses on canvas while a construction tool is armed; first corrected native run 2/2 green (8.5/8.7s). items.title: Angled Build and room-plan ghosts stay on old tile after camera turn
items.body:
﻿## Reproduction
At 1920×1080, arm square Build or a room template, leave the pointer stationary over the map, then turn/tilt/zoom the angled camera using the keyboard or HUD. The preview remains attached to the old world square while the next click is picked from the new camera pose. A mirrored four-cell row can appear under the cursor but place at another origin.

## Observed evidence
- Square Build browser harness: hover at (1100,580), yaw 0°/elevation 45° targets tile (5,4). Change the pose to yaw 37°/elevation 25° without moving the pointer. Before the scene fix, preview still targets (5,4), while the click should target (6,3). A production mutation removing preview repaint reproduced the mismatch; the corrected Full HD test passes.
- Room plan bridge: stationary-cursor mirrored row reproduced a ghost polygon that did not contain the cursor after KeyE; the bridge test was red with old x=25 versus expected x=29. Its separate patch recalculates the pick on camera change.

## Acceptance
- Hover previews for ordinary square Build and room plans reproject from the current screen pointer whenever the camera pose changes, even without a mousemove.
- A click at that pointer commits the same square/origin shown in the preview; construction footprint and costs do not change.
- Validate at intermediate angles, all four drag directions, and map edges in Full HD. Keep keyboard/HUD/mouse camera controls working.

## Implementation checkpoints
- Square Build scene and Full HD tests: `cca1705343` on `codex/oblique-angle-build-qa-20261001` (2/2 browser green; test red under preview-repaint mutation).
- Room-template bridge: `c0ac4b751f` on `codex/room-row-camera-qa-20261001` (stationary-cursor mirrored-row browser proof; further test checkpoint pending).

Related scope: #1585 and #1586. This is a distinct camera-pose synchronization defect, not the asynchronous reply race in #1606.

items.body:
## Verified native mouse acquisition defect

Actual built Cloudflare-served client, Chromium,1920×1080, a new paused prison, Build open and removal armed. Click the visible existing View SELECT with the physical mouse. items.title: Just-in-time materials makes ADR 0075's hard lock reachable by a drag gesture: wall 312 leaves 40
items.body:
Reported out of the #627 work (PR #640), measured rather than reasoned. This is an **economy policy** question, so it is filed rather than decided.

## The measurement

Once a build order buys its own materials at the press (#627 / ADR 0017 decision 7), a wall segment costs **80** minor units — 2 bricks at 40 from `src/content/procurement-catalog.ts:100`, per `src/simulation/construction/definition.ts:89`.

The starting treasury is **25,000**.

```
floor(25_000 / 80) = 312 wall segments, leaving 40
```

**40 is below 65**, which is the figure ADR 0075's own second case names as *"a positive balance on the status strip, and below the 65 that would end this"*. So:

- the prison is **locked on wall 312**;
- the **first thing the game says about money is on wall 313**.

The integration case in #640 asserts all three numbers and confirms the lock by having a plank purchase refused.

## Why this is new

Before #627 a wall order **cost nothing**, so no amount of dragging could reach the lock at all. The lock existed only for players who used the procurement panel deliberately. Now a single sustained drag reaches it.

This is exactly the shape the owner's standing directive is about — *"gra ma być łatwa przyjazna do grania"*. A player who drags a long wall and then finds the game silently unwinnable has been given no signal.

## Why #640 does not fix it

ADR 0075 has **three Accepted decisions** and **none of them is built**. They are the answer to this. Putting a reserve floor, a drag-cost preview, or a low-balance warning into `JustInTimeMaterialsService` would be **economic policy decided inside implementation code**, which `AGENTS.md` reserves to the owner.

## The shape of the options, for whoever decides

1. **Build ADR 0075's decisions** — the existing accepted answer; the largest piece of work, and the only one that is not a new decision.
2. **Warn before the gesture commits** — show the total cost of a drag while it is being dragged, so 312 walls is a number the player saw. Cheapest; does not prevent the lock.
3. **A reserve floor** — refuse a just-in-time purchase that would take the balance below some threshold, so the order parks in `materials-pending` instead of emptying the treasury. Prevents the lock; is new economic policy and needs an ADR.
4. **Raise the starting treasury** — moves the wall number, does not remove the cliff.

Blocked on the owner. Not started.

items.title: Identity stage 3: HUD shell — collapse, resize, layout memory
items.body:
Stage 3 of #1155. Full text: [`docs/IDENTITY_V5_ROLLOUT.md`](../blob/main/docs/IDENTITY_V5_ROLLOUT.md) §"Stage 3". Blocked by **stages 0 and 1**. Gates **stages 4 and 5**.

## Measured state

`alerts` and `minimap` collapse through `collapsedPanels` (`src/ui/hud/hud-state.ts:43`, initial value `:82`), **in memory only** — nothing writes it anywhere. There is no drag-resizable separator anywhere in `src/ui/`: the only `aria-valuenow` is `src/ui/primitives/segmented-bar.ts:199`, a progress bar.

## What the direction adds

- Collapse arrows on the left navigation, the right inspector and the top metric strip, with the handle still reachable after collapse (constitution article 16).
- Drag-resize with real limits: left 72–180 px; right 260–600 px on desktop, bounded so the map keeps its space; on phones a height drag from 180 px to roughly 66 % of the viewport with a 210 px reserve.
- Keyboard parity on the separator: arrows 10 px, Shift+arrows 40 px, Home/End to the extremes, Enter to collapse, double-click to the default. The W3C window-splitter pattern is the reference — and the delivery notes the pattern's own review is unfinished, so it is an implementation hint, **not an accessibility certificate**.
- A Layout menu: slider, reset, "map only", and the clock reachable even when the metric strip is hidden.
- Layout preferences persisted under their **own** key, separate from the save (article 13).

## The rule that makes this stage dangerous — article 17, a gesture has one owner

A resize drag must not pan the camera or place a building. A scroll inside a panel must not move the map. A drag that starts on a panel must not build underneath it. `pointercancel` and lost pointer capture must end the gesture. **`src/input/` already owns the pointer and touch tiers — the resize handle belongs inside that abstraction, not beside it.**

## Evidence required

Browser specs at all three device widths plus an explicit pointer-cancel case and a cursor-leaves-the-window case. `tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts` is where the shell's specs live; it sorts first and carries the slow ones, so budget for that.

## Exit criteria

- Every panel collapses and restores with its handle reachable; focus never lands inside a hidden panel.
- Resize works by pointer, by keyboard and by the slider, with identical limits.
- Layout preferences survive a reload and are absent from the save payload.
- No gesture on a panel reaches the world. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm test:browser` green.

items.title: A player can pan into solid black and there is nothing telling them the way back
items.body:
Measured in PR #792.

## What is there now

**Panning has no clamp.** Grepped all of `world-scene.ts`: only `ZOOM_BOUNDS` bounds anything. **No "return to prison" control exists** anywhere in `src/ui` or `src/rendering`. `frameCameraOnFirstWorld` centres the camera **exactly once**, at the start — which `world-scene-input.spec.ts`'s own #202 docblock already says out loud.

So a player who drags far enough gets a **solid black screen, with the HUD still reading normally, and nothing on it indicating which direction their prison is.**

## What was measured, and the distinction that matters

The pan is **deterministically reversible**: 3,200px out and 3,200px back by pixel-exact drags returns the origin identically.

That is exactly the wrong reassurance. **Reversible by a machine that remembers the precise drag is not the same as recoverable by a player**, who has no record of how far they went or in which direction, and whose only cue — the world itself — is the thing that has gone.

## Why this is not obviously one fix

Three shapes, and they are not equivalent:

1. **Clamp the pan** so the world can never fully leave the viewport. Cheapest, and it removes the state entirely — but it also removes the ability to look at empty land the player may be about to expand into.
2. **A "return to prison" control.** Keeps free panning and makes the state recoverable; costs a control on a HUD that already covers 44% of the canvas at 1280×720 (#792).
3. **Show something at the edge** — a marker pointing home, or keeping the owned chunk faintly visible. Most informative, most work.

The choice depends on whether free panning over unowned land is a feature worth keeping, which is a design question rather than a bug fix. Reported, not built.

## Related

- PR #792 — the measurement and the screenshots
- The companion finding on pointer coverage, which bears directly on option 2's cost
- #202 — where `frameCameraOnFirstWorld`'s once-only behaviour is documented

items.title: Arming a Bed says "Click a tile edge to place a wall" — one hint key serves all 21 buildables, and the view model already knows better
items.body:
Found by playing. **DEFECT**, and the only finding in that pass that *actively misleads* rather than merely withholding.

## What happens

Arm a **Bed**, a **Toilet** or a **Storage Rack** and the hint reads:

> Click a tile edge to place a wall. Drag along it to lay a run. Two fingers, the middle button or the arrow keys still move the camera.

A bed does not go on a tile edge and there is no run to lay. Verified: `src/content/default-locale-en.ts:1087` holds **one** `hud.build.arm-hint` key, swapped only for Remove.

## The information to fix it is already there

`src/ui/hud/view-model.ts:644` carries `occupiesEdge: boolean` per row, and its own docblock at `:635` discusses a row reaching `place-build-order` with `occupiesEdge: false`. So the panel already knows which of the two gestures a given buildable takes; it simply does not ask.

`hud.rooms.arm-hint` (`:1738`) is the precedent for a second, shape-specific hint: *"Drag a rectangle across the tiles this room should cover."*

## Why this one matters more than its size

Walls are **edge** geometry and objects are **tile** geometry, and that distinction is the single least obvious thing about building in this game — it is why four drags around a rectangle behave differently from a drag across its middle (see #892, where the premise that four drags do not enclose was refuted and a mid-line tie-break was found instead). **The one sentence that could teach that distinction currently teaches the wrong half of it to two thirds of the catalogue.**

## What is owed

**The copy is the owner's** under `AGENTS.md`'s fourth exclusion, and it is two sentences rather than one:

1. For an edge-occupying buildable, what the current sentence already says.
2. For a tile-occupying one, what it must convey: that it goes on a tile rather than a boundary, and that it is one press rather than a drag.

**No sentence has been authored.** The wiring — reading `occupiesEdge` and choosing the key — is mine, and it should not land before the words, because a hint that is merely *absent* for a bed is better than one that is wrong.

items.title: A build press landing on `.hud-zoom`/`.hud-minimap` chrome is swallowed with no feedback — and the region is not a fixed band: it grows with the alerts list, ~396px to ~752px tall
items.body:
Filed by the integrator after having it measured, because the handover it came from describes it in terms that would send the next reader at the wrong defect.

## The claim this replaces

The 2026-09-06 handover says: *"The `.hud__corner` occlusion band (roughly x 0–420, y 230–820 at 1440×900) silently eats wall drags — measured in #1038, never filed."* That sentence is a paraphrase of #1038's body, which paraphrases `docs/research/2026-09-06-can-you-name-the-room.md:126-136` — whose own "weakest claims" section explicitly leaves it **unresolved** whether the occlusion is a defect or a layout. The handover dropped that caveat, and two things went wrong on the way.

**1. Half of what it describes is already fixed and gated.** A drag that *starts on the canvas* and crosses or ends under a HUD island builds every tile it drew. The mechanism is `canvas.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)` on the canvas's own `pointerdown` (`src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts:507-511`); capture redirects the browser's compatibility mouse events to the canvas regardless of what is visually on top. It is gated by `tests/browser/world-scene-drag-under-the-hud.spec.ts` (#878), and **the integrator re-ran that gate rather than trusting the report**:

```
✓ builds every segment it drew at 1440x900 (#878)
✓ builds every segment it drew at 1280x720 (#878)
✓ builds every segment it drew at 1920x1080 (#878)   3 passed (2.6m)
```

Filing "wall drags are eaten under the HUD" would be re-reporting a closed defect.

**2. "x 0–420, y 230–820" is not a CSS constant. It is a snapshot of one session's alert count.** The bottom edge is fixed (`align-self: end`, `grid-area: middle`); the top climbs as `.hud-alerts__list` grows, capped only by the middle row's own `max-height: 100%` (`src/ui/hud/hud.css:229-262`, `:274`, `:337-360`). Driven synthetically by appending rows:

| alert rows | corner top | corner height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 434.8 | 396 |
| 4 | 339.8 | 491 |
| 8 | **211.8** | 619 |
| 12 | 83.8 | 747 |
| 16 | 78.5 | 752 (ceiling — butts against the status strip) |

The handover's `y 230` matches the 8-row row of that table almost exactly, which is the likeliest reading of where #1038's number came from. **The worst case is therefore materially worse than the number that was handed over**, not better.

## What the live defect actually is

Not hit-testing. A press that *lands* on a HUD island is kept by that island, and that is deliberate, documented behaviour — `world-scene.ts:472-481` states it in its own words: *"An island still takes a press that lands on it: capture is claimed from a `pointerdown` on the canvas, so a press that starts on the Build panel is never captured and the panel keeps it."*

The defect is one level down, in **DOM/CSS granularity**. `src/ui/hud/hud.css:59-65` grants `pointer-events: auto` to whole panels:

```css
/* Every interactive island opts back in. */
.hud-strip,
.hud__corner > *,
.hud__aside > *,
.hud__side > *,
.hud-tabs__inner {
  pointer-events: auto;
```

`.hud__corner` itself is correctly transparent to the pointer — its padding gaps fall through to the canvas, verified at (200,438) and (100,497), both returning CANVAS. But `.hud__corner > *` means the whole of `.hud-zoom` and the whole of `.hud-minimap` opt in, **including their blank background, their header and their padding**. Probes at (20,570) and (370,620) — inert `.ui-panel__body` chrome, no control — return the panel div with `pointer-events: auto`.

So the build tool's press dies on pixels that look like nothing and do nothing.

## What the player gets

Real press-move-release at three points (the zoom button, the minimap surface, the panel's `<h2>`), read off the worker tee and the Build panel's own `wall-brick` arm:

```
commands before=0 after=0 new=[]     (all three points)
refusalVisible=false  refusalText=""
consoleLines=[]
```

**Nothing is charged** — no `PlaceBuildOrder` is ever submitted, so no money and no materials are lost. It is not uniformly silent, though, and the split matters: over `.hud-zoom__out` and `.hud-minimap__surface` the cursor becomes `pointer` and the gesture *does something else* (the button zooms the camera; the surface has its own `onMinimapNavigate` handler, #793) — the player gets an action they did not ask for. Over inert chrome the cursor stays `auto` and there is **zero** affordance and zero feedback.

## Extent, measured

Viewport sweep at 100% scale, fresh state (no alerts):

```
1440x900: x[0,422] y[434.8,830.8]
1280x720: x[0,422] y[254.8,650.8]
900x600 : x[0,422] y[134.8,530.8]
375x812 : display:none
```

Width is a constant 422px above the breakpoint, because `.hud-minimap` is `width: calc(396px * var(--ui-scale))` (`hud.css:335`) and does not track the viewport. **Below 721px the whole region is gone** — `hud.css:4249` is `.hud__corner { display: none; }` inside `@media (max-width: 720px)`, confirmed. Nothing to fix at 375×812.

Interface-scale sweep at 1440×900:

```
 75%: x[0,317] y[549.1,847.1]  h=298
100%: x[0,422] y[434.8,830.8]  h=396
150%: x[0,632] y[206.2,798.2]  h=592
175%: x[0,737] y[135.1,781.9]  h=647
200%: x[0,842] y[154.0,765.6]  h=612   (height shrinks vs 175%: the corner's own max-height:100% cap starts binding)
```

At 200% the region's width alone is 58% of the viewport.

## Verified by the integrator rather than taken on report

`hud.css:59-65` (`.hud__corner > *`, not `.hud__corner`), `hud.css:4249` (the 720px hide), `hud.css:335` (the fixed 396px width), `world-scene.ts:472-481` (a landing press is the island's, deliberately) and `world-scene.ts:503-513` (`setPointerCapture` on the canvas's `pointerdown`) were each opened and read. The #878 gate was re-run, output above.

## Stated as inference, not measurement

- That #1038's session had accumulated ~6–8 alert rows when it took its numbers. The growth mechanism is reproduced; that particular session's row count is not.
- Whether ordinary play reaches the ceiling case (16+ rows, the region climbing to the status strip). The mechanism is confirmed; the frequency in real play is not.

## What this issue does not decide

It does not say the fix is per-control `pointer-events`. Narrowing the opt-in from the panel to its controls is the obvious candidate and it is not free — a panel that scrolls needs its own body to take the pointer, and `hud.css:59-65`'s comment already ties `touch-action: auto` to exactly that. Whether the alerts list should be allowed to grow to 752px over the world at all is a second question and probably the bigger one.

items.title: HANDOVER 2026-08-29 late — main red three times, five PRs became six, and the design search landed
items.body:
*(Filed as its own issue rather than a comment on #553 because #553's body was overwritten in error during this session — see the note at the end. Everything below is the state a fresh session should assume.)*

`main` merged **#583** and is at v0.0.209-ish. Written against `d47edfd`.

## Gates

**`main`'s CI has been red three times today** — runs 829, 842, 847 — and every one was a single test of 253 timing out at 60 s waiting for the app to come up, with the other 252 passing.

**Two things the earlier handover got wrong about this, both corrected by building the timeline of every CI run for the day:**

1. **Runs 829 and 842 overlapped no other CI run at all.** This workflow chains its jobs with `needs:`, so one job runs at a time per run. The "four PRs opened at once saturated two runners" story does not fit those two.
2. **The `main`-only asymmetry is not significant.** 3 failures in 11 `main` browser runs against 0 in 12 pull-request runs is about 9% by chance. Neither story is established.

**What the artifact does say.** The whole of run 847's `error-context.md` is `- main "Lockstate game application"` — `index.html` and nothing else, so no part of `/src/main.ts` ran. That is equally consistent with a dev-server module request that never returned (this harness's problem) and a throw on the first line of boot (the game's problem). **Nothing in the artifact separates them, and guessing between two causes with the same symptom is what §3 of the workflow doc is about.**

**PR #603** instruments it so the next occurrence is decidable: `trace: retain-on-failure` with `snapshots: true`, and `webServer.stdout: 'pipe'`. Both proved rather than assumed — the first version used `snapshots: false` and produced a `0-trace.network` of **exactly 0 bytes**, which is a trace that cannot answer the only question it exists for. Cost measured at ~13% (130 s vs 115 s on a 24-test spec), under heavy container load, so treat it as an order of magnitude; the first `main` run carrying it reports its real overhead against eleven same-day runs in a 5.5–6.0 min band.

**The anchor is fine.** #583 moved it from `e1813b7` (v0.0.201) to `cfab558` (v0.0.208), so the budget is ~0 of 10 again with four PRs still queued.

## The five PRs were not all green, and two failed on assertions

The earlier handover said all five were green when opened. **#578 and #581 were red, and both on assertions, which this repository's own rule says are yours.**

- **#581** — `arrivedCount is 0, expected exactly 21`. Not what it looked like. `LocomotionStore.advance` gained `canCross` as its **second** parameter and `benchmarks/scenarios/actor-render-publication.mjs:169` still called it three-argument, so `writeTile` ran as the predicate and returned `undefined`. Fixed and green. **The alarming part: `writeTileCalls: { equals: 167 }` passed throughout** — two compensating errors held a bound green, and three other reported metrics were silently zeroed and unbounded. Root class filed as **#602**: `benchmarks/**` and `scripts/**` are outside `tsconfig.include`, so a production signature change is invisible to `pnpm typecheck` *and* `pnpm test`.
- **#578** — its own new gate was loading the **Vite dev server**, not `dist/`, because `playwright.config.ts`'s `testMatch` collected the artifact spec too. Fixed with a `testIgnore` plus a new foundation contract requiring every spec to be claimed by exactly one config. **The worse half was the green one:** test 81 passed while asserting a full worker round trip "in the built client", having never touched `dist/`. Also fixed there: `node scripts/cloudflare-task.mjs build production` aborts inside a worktree with `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` — the same `pnpm exec` trap `playwright.config.ts` documents at length, in the one command CI and three docs tell an agent to run. `scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh` has five surviving instances, reported and not fixed.

**Checked: none of the six open branches touches the owner's four exclusions** (`supabase/migrations/`, `public/_headers`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `wrangler.jsonc`). #578 does change `ci.yml`, which is what the owner's LS-01 ruling asked for.

**Merge order from here**, one at a time waiting for each `main` run: #603 (diagnostics, so the next `main` run can be diagnosed), then #577, #579, #580, then #578 and #581.

## The design search landed

Nineteen models answered the economy brief. Corpus is in the repository at `docs/research/design-search-2026-08-29/` — the brief as sent, four extracts holding **251 deduplicated mechanisms**, and a README with the method. Filed as **#584** (umbrella) and #585–#602.

**The convergence is about order, not ideas.** Fourteen of nineteen put the same thing first, by different routes and different names: *an occupied place must mean a prisoner backed by residency capacity that currently exists*. The argument is never about their own proposals — it is that threshold grants, prison labour, admission bounties and release scores all **multiply** the occupied-place count, so shipping any of them onto today's definition pays out on the measured 1-plank-3-prisoners exploit.

**Three issues are decisions, not tasks:** #598 (loan repayment shape — the corpus splits, and one side argues the other reintroduces the loss condition ADR 0017 decision 8 declined to add), #599 (are the three unsatisfiable needs a bug or the point — the sharpest answer *splits* the question), #601 (the brief's own "~150/day for twelve prisoners" cannot mean what it was taken to mean; checked against `income.ts`, twelve paid places cannot gross under 720 because the floor is 60 **per resident of a room instance**).

## Scheduled work

Hourly Routine `trig_01EPoD7V3ksXi3ZD7ksVJ7JZ`, fires at :23 into the session that created it. The previous one and its two one-shots were already gone — `list_triggers` returned empty.

## The mistake in this session, recorded because the record is the point

**I overwrote #553's issue body without reading it first.** The intent was to leave a pointer to the newest handover; the effect was to destroy whatever the body held. Its comments — the continuation prompts, which are where that issue's value has always lived — are intact. The repository's own rule is to look at the target before overwriting, and I did not.

items.title: [RETRACTED] The game explains why zoning failed, in a box that is 0 pixels tall — and nothing points at it
items.body:
Found by a **mouse-only** playtest of the route a new player actually walks — no keyboard shortcuts — on `main` at `6c309fc` (v0.0.200), Chromium at 1440×900, driving the real page (`index.html` + `src/main.ts`).

This is the strongest candidate yet for the owner's original complaint: *"nie mogłem postawić więzienia … grając sam"*.

## What happens

Rooms → Cell → "Draw on map" → drag a 4×4 → the button reads **"Designate 4 × 4"** and is live. Pressing it sends:

```json
{"type":"ZoneRoom","roomId":"room.cell","x":17,"y":17,"width":4,"height":4}
```

and the worker answers:

```json
{"refusal":{"sequence":14,"tick":0,"reason":"zone.not-enclosed"}}
```

`ROOMS` stays `0`. Every later `PlaceObject` is then refused `place-object.outside-room`. **Nothing on screen changes at any point.**

The explanation *is* produced, and it is correct:

```json
[{"id":"refusal-14",
  "text":"The room was not zoned — this room type must be enclosed, and the area you drew is open on at least one side.Warning",
  "boxWidth":0,"boxHeight":0}]
```

## Why, in three lines that are each defensible alone

| line | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `src/ui/hud/hud-state.ts:51-54` | `collapsedPanels: ['alerts']` — Alerts start folded, deliberately: *"The HUD frames the world and must not cover it; a list that is empty most of the time should not hold open a rectangle over the prison to say so."* |
| `src/ui/hud/hud.ts:1239-1248` | that section is built with **no `trailing`** badge, so the folded header carries no count |
| `src/ui/hud/hud.ts:1244` | the only `set-panel-collapsed` for `'alerts'` anywhere in `src/` is the header's own toggle — **nothing ever un-folds it** |

Measured on arrival: `{"headerText":"ALERTS","ariaExpanded":"false","sectionCollapsed":"true","childElementCount":2}`.

**The Build panel already solves this and is the contrast that makes it a defect rather than a taste question.** Its queue section is *also* collapsed when it appears — and passes `trailing: queueCount` (`src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts:1522-1528`), with its own comment saying why: *"a queue then costs this panel a header and a count, and costs it a list only when the player asks for one."* So the folded queue header still reads "1 waiting · 0 being built". The folded Alerts header reads nothing.

**Consequence:** all **40** reasons in `REFUSAL_LABEL_KEYS` (`src/ui/simulation-alerts.ts:33-73`) are dark by default. Not one of them can reach a player who has not thought to expand a section that never asks to be expanded.

## What was checked and withdrawn

**The live "Designate" button is not the defect.** It is deliberate and reasoned at `src/ui/hud/rooms-panel.ts:1164-1190` (#493/#498): `classifyArea` can be stale, so the panel warns — and it *did*, showing `"OPEN ON AT LEAST ONE SIDE"` — and lets the simulation decide. That reasoning ends *"the real simulation still decides"*. **And the decision is delivered through the 0×0 box.** Two defensible decisions composing into a dead end, which is why neither file looks wrong on its own.

## A second, smaller edge in the same place

A Cell prints one block — `"NEEDS AT LEAST 2 × 3 TILES / MUST BE ENCLOSED / NEEDS 1 × BED / NEEDS 1 × TOILET"` — and the four lines behave three different ways: too-small **disables** Designate (`rooms-panel.ts:1567`), not-enclosed leaves it live and refuses silently, and bed and toilet are post-conditions. **Two of the four teach the player "you can add it later"**, which is exactly the wrong lesson to carry into the enclosure line.

## The informed route does work

Buy bricks → fast-forward → four wall runs → *then* zone: `"rooms":1`, `"zoning":{…,"enclosure":"sealed"}`. **The game is finishable; the ordering is the entire difficulty, and nothing states it.**

## Also settled by the same pass, recorded so nobody re-derives it

- **Camera calibration corrected.** Tile (0,0)'s top-left is at **(−304, −574)** at 1440×900, 64 px/tile. The rule is `(viewportW/2 − 1024, viewportH/2 − 1024)` — the camera is centred on world (1024,1024), the *corner* of `NEW_PRISON_ORIGIN_TILE`. The previously recorded `(−224, −512)` is that same rule evaluated at 1600×1024, so it was never wrong, only unlabelled.
- **Save → reload → load of a mouse-built prison loses nothing measurable.** 1 ROOMS, 22,600 FUNDS, day 2 on both sides; the room returns with *"Cell at 12, 12 is missing 1 × Bed"*; the queue returns. Only the Rooms panel's *selection* resets to "Staff Room".
- **Doors and walls reach the worker correctly.** A south-edge drag arrives as `y:16, edge:"north"`; a door as `{"definitionId":"door-wooden","x":12,"y":16,"edge":"north"}`.
- **Touch and pinch: an empty category, with the numbers that establish it.** Tap places on the nearest edge; a two-finger pinch-out zooms (the same screen point resolves `y:13` → `y:15`, ≈3×) and emits **0** stray commands; a one-finger drag lays a run exactly as the hint promises.
- **`object.sink`'s absence is deliberate**, documented at `src/simulation/construction/definition.ts:330`. Not a defect.

## Observations whose cause is *not* established

Stated separately on purpose — these are measurements, not diagnoses.

- **Refusal is a latch.** `state-machine.ts:517` republishes `refusals.last` with every counts message, so at tick 2,334 the payload still carried a `tick:0` refusal. The design is deliberate; whether a stale, undated warning is the right thing to keep showing is a product question, not a bug report.
- One `World renderer: TypeError: Failed to fetch` at `atlas-library.ts:19` during a `reload()` under a 2× clock. **Did not reproduce** across three plain reloads, and `/assets/actors/asset-registry.json` returned `{"ok":true,"status":200}` from the reloaded page each time. Most likely the outgoing page's aborted fetch — **not established**.

## Not reached

Any prison larger than one cell; guards or prisoners in a mouse-built prison; the Security and Regime tabs; the Overview tab beyond its arrival text; viewports other than 1440×900; the Import/Export path.

## The weakest claim, and what would change it

**That the folded Alerts box is *why* the owner could not build a prison.** What was measured is that the explanation renders at 0×0 and that nothing points at it. Nobody observed the owner's session. What would settle it: the owner saying they had Alerts open, or a second player getting past the zone step unaided with it still folded — either moves this from *"this is the wall"* to *"this is a wall"*.

items.title: [Rendering] Build camera, grid and world-screen coordinate shell
items.body:
## Context
The current Phaser scene is only a production bootstrap. Phase 1 needs a renderer-owned camera and grid shell before construction, chunk rendering or selection tools can be implemented. Rendering remains a view over simulation/world data and must not become authoritative gameplay state.

## Goal
Provide a tested camera/grid foundation with explicit world↔screen coordinate conversion that works with resize, zoom, pointer selection and later chunk culling.

## In scope
- Camera pan through semantic actions and pointer drag.
- Cursor-centered wheel/pinch zoom with configurable min/max bounds.
- Stable world-to-screen and screen-to-world conversion utilities.
- Logical tile-grid visualization independent of terrain content.
- Resize/device-pixel-ratio handling without changing logical coordinates.
- Camera state separated from persistent prison simulation state.
- Initial hooks for visible-world bounds used by future chunk culling.

## Out of scope
- Final art assets, terrain rendering or buildings.
- Input remapping implementation owned by Issue #6.
- Mobile-specific HUD layout.
- Chunk storage implementation.
- Persisting camera state in prison saves.

## Dependencies
- Issue #7 testing conventions.
- Issue #6 semantic action contract for keyboard-driven movement.
.

## Architecture notes
- Phaser owns display objects and camera transforms only.
- Selection tools consume logical coordinates returned by the coordinate layer.
- Zoom must preserve the world point under the cursor where practical.
- Grid rendering must be culled/limited to visible bounds rather than creating an unbounded object per tile.
- Camera defaults and user preferences belong to settings, not save-schema gameplay state.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Keyboard/action and pointer pan produce the same camera movement semantics.
- [ ] Wheel and pinch zoom stay inside explicit bounds.
- [ ] Zoom around a pointer preserves the selected world location within a documented tolerance.
- [ ] World↔screen conversion round-trips across representative camera positions and zoom levels.
- [ ] Grid lines/markers remain aligned with integer tile coordinates.
- [ ] Resize and DPR changes do not corrupt logical coordinates.
- [ ] Visible-world bounds are available for later chunk culling.
- [ ] Rendering code does not mutate simulation-owned state.

## Test requirements
- Unit tests for coordinate transforms and zoom clamping.
- Integration test for resize and camera state.
- Pointer-selection test at multiple zoom levels.
- Manual/browser smoke verification on desktop and touch-capable viewport.

## Performance requirements
- Grid visualization scales with the visible viewport, not total theoretical world size.
- Record object/draw-call behavior at min/max zoom; do not set a final budget without measurements.

## Documentation updates
- Document camera coordinate conventions and ownership boundary.
- Update Phase 1 status in `docs/ISSUE_BACKLOG.md`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Camera/grid shell is typed, tested and buildable.
- [ ] Coordinate contract is documented.
- [ ] No gameplay authority is placed in Phaser objects.

items.title: [Accessibility] Establish touch/pointer parity and accessible interaction baseline
items.body:
## Context
Lockstate is desktop-first during early development but is intended for desktop, tablet and mobile web. Core actions cannot depend exclusively on hover, a right mouse button or keyboard shortcuts. The first rendering/input slice therefore needs explicit pointer and accessibility contracts rather than retrofitting them after gameplay tools exist.

## Goal
Define and prove an accessible, device-independent interaction baseline for camera, selection and future construction tools.

## In scope
- Pointer abstraction for mouse, pen and touch.
- One-finger pan, pinch zoom, tap select, drag/box selection hooks and explicit cancel/context actions.
- Gesture arbitration so pan, selection and future placement do not fire simultaneously.
- Keyboard-focus and DOM-control conventions for HUD/menus.
- Reduced-motion and UI-scale preference hooks.
- Status representation that does not rely only on color.
- Minimum target-size and safe-area guidance for touch controls.
- Device-independent action events consumed by renderer/tools.

## Out of scope
- Final phone/tablet HUD layout.
- Complete WCAG audit of unfinished gameplay.
- Final visual design system.
- Input remapping storage owned by Issue #6.
- Implementing construction tools.

## Dependencies
- Issue #6 semantic input layer.
- Issue #10 camera/grid coordinate shell.
.

## Architecture notes
- Browser gesture defaults must be controlled narrowly; avoid globally breaking scrolling or assistive interaction outside the game surface.
- DOM UI remains keyboard navigable even when the world renderer uses Phaser.
- Pointer events are translated into semantic actions/intents before gameplay systems consume them.
- Touch alternatives must exist for context menus and cancellation.
- Accessibility preferences belong to user settings, not prison simulation state.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A touch-only user can pan, zoom, select and cancel on the test scene.
- [ ] Mouse and pen paths generate the same semantic intents where appropriate.
- [ ] Gesture conflicts are deterministic and documented.
- [ ] Keyboard focus can enter, operate and leave DOM controls without being trapped by the game canvas.
- [ ] Core status examples use text/icon/shape in addition to color.
- [ ] Reduced-motion and UI-scale preferences have typed integration points.
- [ ] Touch targets and safe-area behavior are documented and demonstrated.
- [ ] No core interaction requires hover or right-click without an alternative.

## Test requirements
- Pointer-event unit/contract tests.
- Multi-touch gesture tests using synthetic pointer sequences.
- Browser E2E smoke cases once the browser test project is introduced.
- Manual screen-reader/focus-order check for the available DOM shell.

## Performance requirements
- Pointer-move processing must avoid unbounded allocations and unnecessary simulation messages.
- Coalesce high-frequency camera gestures where safe; preserve final pointer state.

## Documentation updates
- Add interaction/accessibility conventions.
- Record deferred full accessibility audit scope.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Device-independent pointer contract is implemented and tested.
- [ ] Accessible interaction rules are documented.
- [ ] Phase 1 tools can be built without desktop-only assumptions.

items.title: [Input] Three of the seven default keyboard bindings are keys that do nothing, the HUD advertises a fourth set that was never bound, and the semantic event stream has no consumer at all
items.body:
Measured against a real Phaser camera in a real Chromium, and confirmed by four surviving mutations. **VERIFIED, LIVE.**

#141 records that `src/input/pointer.ts`, `src/input/accessibility.ts` and the settings-persistence API have no consumer — modules that are simply not wired. This is the sharper half: the parts that **are** wired, to keys a player can actually press, that still do nothing. That is a different defect from an unwired module, because a dead key is indistinguishable from a broken game.

## What a player presses, and what happens

`src/input/bindings.ts:10-18` declares seven default bindings. `src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts:244-250` is the only consumer of any of them:

```ts
    const horizontal = Number(this.keyboard.isActive('camera.right')) - Number(this.keyboard.isActive('camera.left'));
    const vertical = Number(this.keyboard.isActive('camera.down')) - Number(this.keyboard.isActive('camera.up'));
```

`isActive` is called for four action ids and no others. `grep -rn "isActive" src/` outside `src/input/` returns exactly those two lines.

| default binding | action | consumer in `src/` | measured in a browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `KeyW` | `camera.up` | `world-scene.ts:246` | pans |
| `KeyA` | `camera.left` | `world-scene.ts:245` | pans |
| `KeyS` | `camera.down` | `world-scene.ts:246` | pans — `scrollY 0 → 180.89` over 400 ms |
| `KeyD` | `camera.right` | `world-scene.ts:245` | pans — `scrollX 0 → 239.66` over 400 ms |
| `Equal` | `camera.zoom.in` | **none** | **zoom unchanged** |
| `Minus` | `camera.zoom.out` | **none** | **zoom unchanged** |
| `Escape` | `build.cancel` | **none** | **a build run in progress survives it and still commits** |

Executed, against the real `WorldScene` in a real `Phaser.Game` with `Scale.RESIZE` (the same config as `src/main.ts`):

```
ZOOM  before 1 after 1        # five presses of Equal, then five of Minus
```

and, with the build tool armed, a left-press at the canvas centre dragged 200 px right, `Escape` pressed mid-drag, then released:

```
ESCAPE during= [{"tileX":10,"tileY":6,"edge":"north"},{"tileX":11,…}]   # 4 segments targeted
ESCAPE after = [{"tileX":10,"tileY":6,"edge":"north"},{"tileX":11,…}]   # identical
ESCAPE placed count= 1  segments in first= 4                            # the run committed anyway
```

`Escape` changed nothing about the pending run and did not stop it being placed. The scene does have a cancel path — `WorldScene.cancelBuild` (`world-scene.ts:361`) — and it is reachable only from a second finger arriving during a pinch (`:184`) and from the tool being disarmed mid-gesture (`:255-260`). The keyboard is not wired to it.

## The HUD tells the player about a fourth set of keys that was never bound

`src/content/default-locale-en.ts:154`:

```
'hud.build.arm-hint': 'Click a tile edge to place a wall. Drag along it to lay a run. Two fingers, the middle button or the arrow keys still move the camera.'
```

This string is rendered on screen — it is `armHint` in `src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts:186`, painted into the Build panel whenever the map route is shown. `DEFAULT_KEYBOARD_BINDINGS` contains no `Arrow*` code. Measured:

```
N: ArrowRight: scroll 0,0 -> 0,0
N: ArrowLeft:  scroll 0,0 -> 0,0
N: ArrowUp:    scroll 0,0 -> 0,0
N: ArrowDown:  scroll 0,0 -> 0,0
N: KeyS (control): scrollY 0 -> 180.89
```

Each arrow key was held for 400 ms. The camera did not move by one unit on any of them; the control moved 180.89. **VERIFIED.** "the middle button" in the same sentence is true (`world-scene.ts:164-166`). "Two fingers" is plausible from the code and was not exercised in this audit.

This is a player-visible false statement about the controls, in the one place a new player looks for them, and it is worse than the dead `Equal`/`Minus` keys: an unadvertised key that does nothing is a missing feature; an advertised key that does nothing reads as a broken build.

## Nine declared actions, four consumed

`src/input/actions.ts:1-11` declares nine `ACTION_IDS`. Five have no reader anywhere in `src/`: `camera.zoom.in`, `camera.zoom.out`, `selection.primary`, `build.confirm`, `build.cancel`. All nine have a locale entry (`src/content/default-locale-en.ts:172-182`), so the catalog describes a control surface twice the size of the one that exists.

## The `SemanticActionEvent` stream has no consumer at all

`src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts:127-132`:

```ts
    const keyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
      this.keyboard.keyDown(event);
    };
    const keyUp = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
      this.keyboard.keyUp(event);
    };
```

`KeyboardInputAdapter.keyDown`/`keyUp` return `readonly SemanticActionEvent[]`. Both return values are discarded. The adapter's actual production role is a `Set<string>` of held key codes that `isActive` polls; the entire event-construction path in `eventsFor` (`src/input/keyboard.ts:35-41`) runs on every keystroke and its result is thrown away.

`docs/INPUT.md:3` says "Gameplay and camera consumers **receive** semantic action IDs such as `camera.up`". Nothing receives one. The one consumer polls.

## A filter that reads as a rule and is a tautology

`src/input/keyboard.ts:35-41`:

```ts
  private eventsFor(code: string, phase: SemanticActionEvent['phase']): readonly SemanticActionEvent[] {
    const contexts = this.activeContexts();
    return this.bindings
      .filter((binding) => binding.code === code && intersects(binding.contexts, contexts))
      .map((binding) => ({ action: binding.action, phase, source: 'keyboard' as const }))
      .filter((event) => ACTION_REGISTRY[event.action].behavior === 'discrete' || phase === 'started' || phase === 'ended');
  }
```

`phase` is typed `SemanticActionEvent['phase']`, which `src/input/actions.ts:26` defines as `'started' | 'ended'`. So `phase === 'started' || phase === 'ended'` is **unconditionally true** and the predicate can never remove an element. It reads as "continuous actions only emit on a phase boundary" — a rule — and enforces nothing. The `ACTION_REGISTRY[event.action].behavior === 'discrete'` term is never evaluated for its answer.

Proven by a matched pair of mutations, not by reading:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| replace the whole `.filter(…)` at `keyboard.ts:40` with `.map((event) => event)` | **SURVIVED** — 145 files / 1442 passed / 1 skipped |
| narrow the predicate to `ACTION_REGISTRY[event.action].behavior === 'discrete'` (i.e. make it actually discriminate) | **KILLED** — `tests/unit/input.test.ts` › "uses physical movement keys, independently of the keyboard layout" fails |

The pair matters: the first mutation survives *because the predicate is inert*, not because the behaviour is untested. The second shows the suite would catch a filter that did something. This is the "check that reads as protection and is wired to nothing" shape, in its smallest possible form.

## Surviving mutations for the dead bindings

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| delete `{ device: 'keyboard', code: 'Equal', action: 'camera.zoom.in', … }` from `DEFAULT_KEYBOARD_BINDINGS` (`bindings.ts:15`) | **SURVIVED** — 1442 passed |
| delete `{ device: 'keyboard', code: 'Escape', action: 'build.cancel', … }` (`bindings.ts:17`) | **SURVIVED** — 1442 passed |
| `world-scene.ts:72`: `() => ['world']` → `() => ['modal']`, which kills **all** keyboard camera panning | **SURVIVED** — 1442 passed |

The third is the one worth staring at: the single wire between the input tier and the game can be cut and the whole suite stays green. There is no browser test either — no spec under `tests/browser/` sends a key to the world (`grep -rn "keyboard" tests/browser/*.spec.ts` finds two comments and one test about *reaching the numeric fallback* by keyboard, none about the camera), and `WorldScene` is never constructed by any test in the repository (`grep -rn WorldScene tests/` → one comment, `app-shell.spec.ts:833`).

## VERIFIED vs INFERRED

- **VERIFIED** by execution: `Equal`/`Minus` change zoom by nothing; `Escape` does not cancel a pending run and the run commits; all four arrow keys move the camera by nothing while `KeyS` moves it 180.89; `WASD` works; the four surviving mutations and the two killed ones above.
- **VERIFIED** by grep over `src/`: five of nine action ids have no reader; both adapter return values are discarded; `isActive` has two call sites.
- **VERIFIED** by the type declaration: the `eventsFor` predicate's second disjunct is a tautology.
- **INFERRED**: nothing. No claim here rests on reading alone.

## LIVE vs LATENT

**LIVE**, all of it. `+`/`-` and `Escape` are keys a player will try on the first session, and the on-screen hint sends them to the arrow keys. None of it needs a future feature to become a defect.

## The smallest correct fix

These are three separate fixes and only the first is unambiguous.

1. **The hint must not name controls that do not exist.** Either add arrow-key bindings, or correct `hud.build.arm-hint` to name `W`/`A`/`S`/`D`. Correcting the string is the smaller change and does not add a control surface nobody asked for; adding the bindings is the better game. Note that a *third* option is wrong: naming keys in a hard-coded English sentence is already awkward against `docs/INPUT.md:6`, whose whole point is that a label comes from the keyboard-layout map and not from a literal. `resolveKeyboardLabel` (`src/input/bindings.ts:48`) exists for exactly this and has no caller.
2. **`Escape` should cancel.** `WorldScene.cancelBuild` already does the right thing; `update()` needs one `if (this.keyboard.isActive('build.cancel'))` beside the four existing `isActive` calls — but `build.cancel` is a `discrete` action and `isActive` is a held-key poll, so the honest fix is to consume the `keyDown` return value rather than to poll. That is the same change item 3 needs.
3. **Either consume the event stream or delete the zoom bindings.** `camera.zoom.in`/`camera.zoom.out` are `discrete` and cannot be served by a poll at all; a discrete action needs the `SemanticActionEvent` array that `keyDown` returns and `world-scene.ts:128` throws away. Two directions, and they are a real choice:
   - wire the events (`keyDown` returns them; the scene switches on `action`), which makes `bindings.ts`, `ACTION_REGISTRY.behavior` and the `eventsFor` filter all mean something and makes `docs/INPUT.md:3` true; or
   - accept that the camera is polled, delete the three unbound bindings and the five unconsumed action ids with their locale keys, and correct `docs/INPUT.md` to describe a polled camera.

   **This one needs the owner, not an implementation choice.** `AGENTS.md` boundary 10 requires input to "support remapping, QWERTY/AZERTY and touch/pointer interaction", and #141 already flags remapping and accessibility as an unfinished-or-wrong commitment needing owner judgement. Deleting the actions makes boundary 10 harder to satisfy later; wiring them is the larger change. It belongs with #141's question rather than being decided inside `world-scene.ts`.

4. Whichever direction is taken, **delete the tautology** at `keyboard.ts:40`. If the events get consumed it should become a real rule with a test; if they do not, the whole `eventsFor` body is dead and should go with them. Leaving a tautological predicate that looks like a rule is the worst of the three.

## The test that should have caught it

`tests/browser/world-scene-input.spec.ts`, which does not exist. The scene is the only production consumer of `src/input/**` and no test constructs it. A harness that mounts the real `WorldScene` into a real `Phaser.Game` and drives real keys is ~40 lines against the pattern `tests/browser/camera-harness.ts` already establishes; it is how every measurement in this issue was taken, and it would pin, at minimum:

- each bound key moves the camera in the direction it claims (kills the `['world'] → ['modal']` mutation);
- `Equal`/`Minus` change the zoom (currently fails);
- `Escape` clears a pending run (currently fails);
- the keys named in `hud.build.arm-hint` are the keys that work (currently fails).

Headless, `tests/unit/input.test.ts` could additionally assert that every `ACTION_IDS` entry has a reader in `src/` — the same shape as `tests/foundation/unconsumed-content-contract.test.ts` applies to content ids, and it would have caught five of these nine at declaration time.

## Open branches touching the same files

None. `origin/main` is `e24ea85`; `src/input/**`, `src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts` and `src/content/default-locale-en.ts` are untouched by any open PR.

Refs #141 (the unconsumed half of the same tree), #6 (the issue that built this layer), #74 (the build tool that claimed the one-finger drag), `AGENTS.md` boundary 10, `docs/INPUT.md`.

items.title: [Audit] What a player can actually do: one of thirteen systems does observable work, and the shortest path to a loop
items.body:
An end-to-end reachability audit traced from the real composition root (`src/main.ts`) outward, not from the tests. **This question is not answered anywhere else in the repository**, and the answer is short.

Claims are **VERIFIED** (read and/or executed) or **INFERRED**. Executed claims were driven through `createNewSimulationRuntime` and `Kernel.step()` — the same runtime the worker builds — from throwaway scripts outside the repository. Raw output is quoted.

---

## 1. What a player can do today

1. **Load the page and look at an empty grey world.** The worker is `uninitialized`; the strip reads `Day --` and zeros.
2. **Press "New prison".** The only thing on the page that starts a simulation. You get a 32×32 square of dirt with one owned chunk, and a save.
3. **Look at the prison.** Pan with the middle button, WASD or arrows; zoom with wheel, `+`, `−`; one-finger drag and two-finger pinch on touch. **Nothing the camera does reaches the simulation.**
4. **Start and stop time.** Pause / Play / Fast-forward genuinely work. One in-game day is two minutes of real time at ×1.
5. **Switch to Build and choose "Brick wall" or "Wooden door".** The only two entries.
6. **Press "Place on map", then click or drag along a tile edge.** A translucent brown box appears. It is a build *order*.
7. **Watch that box stay translucent forever.** It never becomes a wall — there is no way in the entire interface to buy the bricks it waits for. It survives every save and reload.
8. **Type coordinates instead.** Same outcome. **A coordinate outside the owned chunk is silently discarded** — nothing appears and nothing says why.
9. **Save, load, delete, export.** All work. Export downloads a file the application cannot import back.
10. **`?actors=demo`** shows three scripted sprites walking in a circle. A rendering demonstration, not simulation state.

**That is the complete list.** The single mechanical consequence a player can produce is item 6: a ghost outline.

---

## 2. The proof, executed

`createNewSimulationRuntime(0)`, one `PlaceBuildOrder` exactly as `main.ts` builds it at tile (16,16), then 2,000 ticks — 100 in-game seconds:

```
[A] after 2000 ticks state=materials-pending progress=0 failReason=undefined
[A] treasury=25000
[A] chunk topEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

`[[0,1024]]` is 1,024 run-length-encoded zeroes: **no wall anywhere in the world.**

The same runtime with one `PurchaseMaterials` command inserted first:

```
[B] state=completed treasury=24600
[B] chunk topEdge=[[0,528],[1,1],[0,495]]
```

Index 528 = `16 × 32 + 16` — the exact tile. **The construction pipeline is complete and correct; the only missing link in the whole chain is a producer for one command.**

---

## 3. Thirteen systems run every tick. One does work a player can see.

Read from a live runtime's `systemExecutionOrder`:

| System | Iterates | Non-empty in a reachable session? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prisoners.intake` | live prisoner entities | **No** — `admitPrisoner` has no caller in `src/` |
| `prisoners.needs-decay` | same | **No** (see #259) |
| **`construction`** | `orderedOrders()` | **Yes — the one reachable system.** Stalls at `materials-pending` |
| `procurement` | `this.pending` | **No** — returns on line 156 every tick, 20 times a second, forever |
| `navigation` | graph + queue | **Partially.** `ensureGraph()` does real work; **nothing reads its output** — no route is ever requested |
| `prisoners.actions` | prisoner query | No |
| `operations.jobs` | `activeJobs()` | **No** — `submitCarryItem` has no caller |
| `contraband.intelligence` | decays an empty ledger | No |
| `security.deployment` | `allGuardIds()` | **No** — `GuardRoster.hire` has no caller |
| `security.patrol` | same | No |
| `incidents.trigger` | `sectorIds` (empty) | No |
| `contraband.search` | queued orders (none) | No |
| `incidents.response` | `openIncidents()` | No |

**Eleven of thirteen iterate permanently empty collections.** One more does real computation nothing reads.

### Three subsystems are not even registered

- **`TopologyManager`** (229 lines) is constructed, exposed on `SimulationRuntime.topology`, and **`update()` is never called anywhere in `src/`**. It has no `id`/`order`/`schedule`, **so it cannot be registered with the kernel at all.** Room enclosure detection never runs.
- **`UtilityNetwork`** — two instances built, no `update`, and `addNode`/`connect`/`evaluate` have no caller outside their own module.
- **`ContainerRegistry`, `JobBoard`, `JobWorkerPool`** — built empty; only the construction container is registered and nothing is ever put in it.

---

## 4. Three findings worth their own attention

### A finished wooden door writes nothing and creates no door

`edgeNumericIdFor` returns `0` for `category: 'object'`, so `finalizeConstruction` only bumps the geometry revision. Executed:

```
[C] door state=completed
[C] topEdge=[[0,1024]]  leftEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

It exists only as a 0.55-tile-high brown slab drawn from the order list. `DoorRegistry.register` is called from exactly one place — restoring from a snapshot. **Nothing creates the first door.**

### A refused order gives the player no feedback of any kind

The command reply acknowledges *receipt*, not effect: `state-machine.ts:524-535` posts `status: 'queued'` as soon as the kernel accepts it. A `failReason` of `out-of-bounds` or `unowned-land` is mapped to `undefined` by `phaseOf` and drawn as nothing. Executed, typing `100, 100` into fields that have no `min`/`max`:

```
[E] far order state=failed failReason=out-of-bounds
```

The refusal line stays hidden because the command *was* queued successfully, and no ghost appears. (`x = 2e9`, `x = -5`, `x = 9e12` all fail cleanly — **no player-reachable crash was found down any path.**)

### `ConstructionSystem` has a complete undo/redo model that nothing can reach

`undo()`/`redo()` are transaction-grouped and snapshot-safe; `main.ts:492` mints one `transactionId` per gesture *specifically* so a twelve-segment wall undoes as one. There is no control, no binding and no intent that can trigger it — `grep` for `KeyZ`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey` in `src/` returns **zero matches**.

Five of six commands have no producer: `PurchaseMaterials`, `CancelBuildOrder`, `Undo`, `Redo`, `ZoneRoom` — and `ZoneRoom`'s consumer is itself a no-op (`case 'ZoneRoom': break;`).

---

## 5. Where each on-screen number comes from

Fresh session, before any tick:

```
[D] {"prisoners":0,"prisonersInIntake":0,"prisonersHighRisk":0,"staff":0,
     "staffUnassigned":0,"rooms":0,"roomCapacity":0,"roomOccupants":0,
     "activeIncidents":0,"contrabandDiscovered":0,"treasuryMinorUnits":25000}
```

| On screen | Real or constant? |
| --- | --- |
| **Prisoners** | Real projection, **permanently 0** |
| Cell occupancy bar | **Never rendered** — `prisonerCapacity` is hard-coded `0` on the main thread, so the bar is removed |
| **Staff** / **Rooms** / **Incidents** / **Contraband** | Real projections, all permanently 0 |
| **Funds** | Real value, **effectively a constant 25,000** — nothing credits it and the only spender is unreachable |
| **Day N** and **% through the day** | **Real and moving.** The only figures that change |
| **Alerts** | **Always "No active alerts."** `viewModel.alerts` is assigned nowhere except a literal `[]` |
| **Minimap** | **Constant string** "Minimap is not available yet" |
| **World canvas** | Real. **Actors are always empty** — the feed's own comment says the bundle *does* carry prisoner tile positions and this feed does not decode them |

**Two projections produce nothing anyone reads:** `projectWorldForRendering` has no consumer at all — the renderer decodes the *save bundle's* world section instead, so the purpose-built render projection is dead and the save format is doing its job. And `projectStatusStrip`'s `clock` and `regime` blocks are computed and discarded.

---

## 6. The built/reachable line, measured

**207 of 256 `.ts` files under `src/` are reachable from the composition root; 49 are not.** Excluding barrels, the 29 substantive never-imported modules total **3,978 lines**: all of `services/telemetry/`, `services/entitlements/`, `services/challenges/`, `persistence/cloud/`, and three presentation projections.

**Reachable-but-never-called exports**, each verified by grep: `TopologyManager.update`, `admitPrisoner`, `GuardRoster.hire`, `JobBoard.submitCarryItem`, `UtilityNetwork.addNode/connect/evaluate`, `resolveEscapeOpportunity`, `buildRiotRegimeSchedule`, `toIncidentAlert`, `summarizeIncidents`, nine of the ten presentation projections, `remapKeyboardBinding`, `saveInputSettings`, `loadAccessibilitySettings`, `SessionController.importInto`.

**Content:** 62 declared ids, **53 with no reference in `src/` outside `src/content/`**. The nine that have one are all referenced by a system that never runs on live data. Zero contraband categories, zero security grades, zero staff roles and zero object ids are referenced from `src/` at all.

**One unused message key:** `HUD_MESSAGE_KEY.buildNote` is declared and never rendered — the only one of 56 with no render site. Its English is *"An order is queued now and built while the clock runs."* Given §2, it is fortunate it is not on screen.

---

## 7. The shortest path to a playable loop, ordered

Wiring only. No new architecture, no ADR, no new abstraction.

**Step 1 — Make a placed wall become a wall.** The highest-value change in the repository; everything downstream is proven to work. **The owner has chosen the surface: a quantity stepper on the Build panel** (not the auto-purchase this audit first sketched). That work is in flight. What the player gets: the ghost turns solid, and the **Funds** chip drops. Two of six status numbers start moving. It also makes insolvency visible — 25,000 buys 156 walls, and `spend` refuses rather than overdrawing — which leads straight to step 2.

**Step 2 — Tell the player when the simulation refuses.** Without it, "out of money" is indistinguishable from today's bug. Two facts currently vanish: `PurchaseOutcome` is discarded at `session-commands.ts:42` (the code says so), and `failReason` never leaves the simulation. The machinery already exists and has **never had a producer**: `HudViewModel.alerts` is fully implemented, with severity badges and an empty-state row. Publish a small refusal field on the existing `simulation/status-counts` channel — no new message kind — and map it in `main.ts`'s existing listener.

**Step 3 — Make `ZoneRoom` register a room instance.** Its handler is `break;`. `RoomInstanceRegistry.register` takes exactly what the command carries plus a capacity and capability list. **Do this before step 4:** `IntakeSystem` marks an arrival `'failed'` when no instance of the required room type exists *at all*, so admitting into a prison with no cell is a structural dead end, not a wait.

**Step 4 — Admit one prisoner.** Executed proof that the rest is ready — one `room.cell` registered, `admitPrisoner` called, 600 ticks:

```
entity=0 intakeStage=4 (completed)
metrics={"completedCount":1,"failedCount":0,"accommodationBacklogTicks":0}
counts={"prisoners":1,...,"rooms":1,"roomCapacity":1,"roomOccupants":1,...}
position=10,10  (the cell's anchor tile)
```

**Two calls turn three of the six status numbers real.** Fix #259 in the same change, or the prisoner is inert.

**Step 5 — Decode actors into the render frame.** `actors: []` is one line, and the feed's comment says the data is already in the bundle. `ActorLayer` is built, the atlases load, and `DemoActorFeed` proves the sprite path end to end. **This is the moment the prison stops being a diagram.**

**Step 6 — Reach the undo that already exists.** A binding plus a case, and a fully built feature returns.

---

## What is deliberately not claimed

- The page was not run in a browser. Every DOM/Phaser statement is from source and marked INFERRED; every simulation statement marked VERIFIED was executed.
- A passing test was never treated as evidence a player can reach something. Where a test is the only consumer, that is what is said.
- **No player-visible consequence is attributed to any unreachable subsystem.** `TopologyManager` never running, telemetry being unwired and 53 unconsumed ids cost a player nothing *today* — precisely because there is no loop for them to be part of. The finding is the gap between built and reachable, not an invented symptom.

items.title: [Docs] Five claims in docs/INPUT.md are false against the code at e24ea85, and no assertion covers that file
items.body:
`docs/INPUT.md` is 17 bullets long. Five of them state something the code does not do. Each is checked below against `e24ea85`, with the grep or the executed observation that settles it.

`tests/foundation/documentation-claims-contract.test.ts` — the file whose whole purpose is "documentation claims about the code, asserted against the code", written after #121 found five false sentences in `ARCHITECTURE.md` — mentions `docs/INPUT.md` nowhere. So none of these had anything to become false against.

Three of the five are the *documentation half* of defects filed separately (#199, #200, #201); they are listed here as well because correcting the prose is a different change from fixing the code, and because a reader of `docs/INPUT.md` today is misled about what the input tier does whether or not those issues get worked.

---

## 1. Line 3 — "Gameplay and camera consumers **receive** semantic action IDs such as `camera.up`"

**VERIFIED FALSE.** No consumer receives one. `KeyboardInputAdapter.keyDown`/`keyUp` return `readonly SemanticActionEvent[]`, and the only production caller discards both (`src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts:127-132`):

```ts
    const keyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
      this.keyboard.keyDown(event);
    };
```

The camera *polls* held keys instead (`world-scene.ts:245-246`, two `isActive` calls covering four of the nine declared action ids). `grep -rn "SemanticActionEvent" src/` returns nine hits, all inside `src/input/`: the type is produced and never consumed anywhere.

Correct wording: the camera reads held-key state through `isActive`; the `SemanticActionEvent` stream has no consumer yet. See #200 for the choice about which of those two should survive.

## 2. Line 6 — "User-facing labels use the browser keyboard-layout map when available; the deterministic fallback is the physical-code label."

**VERIFIED FALSE as a present-tense statement.** There are no user-facing key labels. `resolveKeyboardLabel` (`src/input/bindings.ts:48`) and `fallbackKeyboardLabel` (`:41`) have exactly three references in `src/`, all three inside `bindings.ts` itself (the two declarations and `resolveKeyboardLabel` calling the fallback on line 60). Nothing in `src/rendering/**`, `src/ui/**` or `src/main.ts` imports either.

The one place a key is named to the player names it in prose instead: `src/content/default-locale-en.ts:154` (`hud.build.arm-hint`) says "the arrow keys still move the camera", which is both hard-coded and false — see #200.

Correct wording: the label resolver exists and is tested (`tests/unit/input.test.ts:49-53`); nothing displays a key label yet.

## 3. Line 8 — "`text-entry` is deliberately absent from world action defaults, **preventing game controls from firing while a text field owns input**."

**VERIFIED FALSE**, by execution: with a real `<input type="text">` focused and receiving the character, holding `KeyD` typed `"d"` into the field *and* panned the camera 249.6 world units. `'text-entry'` is never in the active-context set, because `world-scene.ts:72` is the constant `() => ['world']`. Filed with the reproduction as #201.

The clause before the comma is true and worth keeping; the clause after it claims a protection that does not exist.

## 4. Lines 9 and 15 — "Keyboard and the minimal pointer/**touch** adapter emit one `SemanticActionEvent` contract" / "Pointer, touch and **accessibility** adapters emit this same action contract (`src/input/pointer.ts`, `src/input/gestures.ts`, `src/input/accessibility.ts`, Issue #11)"

**VERIFIED FALSE for two of the three named modules.**

- `src/input/gestures.ts` emits `Gesture` (`gestures.ts:19-28`), a `{kind:'pan'|'pinch'}` union of screen-space deltas. It never mentions `SemanticActionEvent`, and `TouchGestureTracker.move` returns `Gesture | undefined`. That is the right design — `docs/INPUT.md:10` describes it correctly two bullets later ("exposes pan deltas and cursor-centered pinch scale") — so lines 9 and 15 contradict line 10 within the same file.
- `src/input/accessibility.ts` is not an adapter and emits nothing. Its four exports are `ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS_VERSION`, the `AccessibilitySettings` interface, `DEFAULT_ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS` and `decodeAccessibilitySettings`. There is no event type, no method, and no `SemanticActionEvent` reference in the file.

Only `src/input/keyboard.ts` and `src/input/pointer.ts` produce `SemanticActionEvent`.

Correct wording: keyboard and pointer share the `SemanticActionEvent` contract; touch emits `Gesture`; accessibility is a versioned settings record with no event surface. Line 13 already says the last part correctly ("Accessibility preferences are a separate versioned user-settings record… validated integration points"), so line 15 also contradicts line 13.

## 5. Line 16 — "Settings persistence goes through an injectable `KeyValueStore`…, **not a hard-coded browser global**… **The browser `main.ts` entry point supplies `window.localStorage`**… corrupted or missing entries **fall back to defaults rather than failing boot**."

**VERIFIED FALSE in two of its three clauses.** `src/main.ts` contains no reference to `localStorage`, to `loadInputSettings`, or to anything under `src/input/` — grep over the whole 418-line file returns zero. The renderer supplies the global, hard-coded, in a class field initializer: `src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts:71`, `loadInputSettings(window.localStorage)`.

And "rather than failing boot" is false for a store that throws: `readJson` (`src/input/storage.ts:36-44`) puts `store.getItem(key)` on line 37, outside its `try`. Executed against the real `index.html` with a throwing `localStorage`: **0 canvases, no HUD, no save panel, one uncaught `SecurityError`, empty `document.body.textContent`.** Filed as #199.

The middle clause is the load-bearing one: an injectable seam that the single production caller bypasses is why the failure is unguarded. Correcting the sentence and correcting the wiring are the same job.

---

## What the file gets right, named individually

Because a doc audit that only lists errors is not a review of the file:

- **Line 5** — "Defaults bind physical `KeyboardEvent.code` positions (`KeyW`, `KeyA`, `KeyS`, `KeyD`), so the same movement cluster works on QWERTY and AZERTY keyboards." **True.** Every entry in `DEFAULT_KEYBOARD_BINDINGS` (`src/input/bindings.ts:10-18`) is keyed by `code`, and `KeyboardInputAdapter` matches on `binding.code === code` (`keyboard.ts:38`) — never on `key`. An AZERTY player gets ZQSD at the same physical positions, which is the AZERTY convention. This is the single most important sentence in the file for `AGENTS.md` boundary 10 and it is correct.
- **Line 7** — "Collisions are rejected only when the same device/code is active in overlapping contexts; mutually exclusive contexts may share a binding." **True**: `findBindingConflicts` keys `seen` by `${device}:${code}:${context}` (`bindings.ts:78`), and `tests/unit/input.test.ts:29-38` asserts both directions.
- **Line 10** — the gesture core's shape. **True.**
- **Line 11** — the pinch carries a midpoint translation as well as a scale. **True**: `gestures.ts:54-61` returns `deltaX`/`deltaY`, and `tests/unit/input.test.ts:101-120` asserts the translations sum to the midpoint's travel and the scales cancel over a pair of moves.
- **Line 12** — build arbitration is modal, not threshold-based, and the middle-drag, wheel and two-finger gestures are camera controls at all times. **True** for the middle button (`world-scene.ts:164-166`) and the wheel (`:136-149`); the arming toggle behaves as described. Note the sentence says "keyboard … are camera controls at all times", which is true only of `WASD` — the `Equal`/`Minus`/`Escape` bindings are inert (#200).
- **Line 13** — accessibility is a separate versioned settings record and belongs nowhere near prison state. **True**, and it contradicts line 15.
- **Line 14** — input settings have their own versioned serialization and are not embedded in a prison snapshot. **True**: `INPUT_SETTINGS_VERSION` is its own constant and no save-schema module references it.
- **Line 17** — "`remapAndPersistKeyboardBinding` composes validation with persistence so a conflicting or invalid remap is never written to storage." **True of the function** (`src/input/storage.ts:63-72`, asserted by `tests/unit/input.test.ts:148-159`). It has no caller in `src/`, which #141 already records; the sentence describes a correct component rather than a shipped behaviour, and that is worth saying explicitly in the doc rather than leaving a reader to assume remapping is available.

## LIVE vs LATENT

**LIVE.** `CLAUDE.md` instructs agents to "use repository docs and ADRs as the source of truth", and #116 records that doc-truth regressions are this repository's dominant defect class precisely because they send an agent in a straight line the wrong way. Claim 5 is the costly one: an agent told that `main.ts` injects the store will look for the injection point and not find the bug; an agent told corrupted entries never fail boot will not test a hostile store.

## The smallest correct fix

1. Rewrite the five bullets to say what the code does. Each correction is one sentence and is spelled out above.
2. Add the mechanically checkable ones to `tests/foundation/documentation-claims-contract.test.ts`, which already has the machinery (`sourceFilesMatching`) and the vacuity guard. Three are cheap and exact:
   - the set of files producing `SemanticActionEvent` is exactly `{keyboard.ts, pointer.ts}` — kills claim 4 the moment it becomes false again;
   - `src/input/accessibility.ts` contains no `SemanticActionEvent`;
   - whichever module supplies `window.localStorage` to `loadInputSettings` is the one the doc names.

   Mutation to prove each assertion, once written: flip the named file in the doc sentence, or add a `SemanticActionEvent` return to `gestures.ts`, and confirm the new test fails.
3. Claims 1, 3 and 5 also have a code half; if #200, #201 and #199 are fixed first, three of these five sentences become true without editing them. Sequencing choice, not a technical one — but if the code is fixed and the prose is not re-read, the file stays wrong in the other direction.

**Not an ADR question.** #200 contains the one genuine decision in this area (whether the semantic event stream gets a consumer or gets deleted); the prose should follow whatever that decides, not pre-empt it.

## Open branches touching the same files

None. `origin/main` is `e24ea85`; `docs/INPUT.md` and `src/input/**` are untouched by any open PR.

Refs #199, #200, #201 (the code halves), #121, #122 (previous doc-truth sweeps), #141, `AGENTS.md` boundary 10.
